description: Fix one base part with a fixed joint, then place every part that touches or attaches to another with joint_create (one call creates the joint and solves placement). Use part_set_transform only for parts that touch nothing. Block-out positions are rough; joints set final positions. Prefer this over hand-computed part_set_transform numbers: one call creates a joint and solves the placement. type is coincident, parallel, perpendicular, distance, angle, concentric, symmetric or fixed (planar is coincident); picks are one row per reference from list_faces (face_id with its key from the same row; a cylindrical face is an axis pick; a face_id is never an ambiguous axis; { part_id } alone is a whole-part pick), one pick for fixed and two for every other type; name, value_mm, sense and opposed as on joint_set_params. Runs the same open → pick → set params → commit path as the Joints card (the advanced path) and records one assembly undo step. The result carries jointId, type, name, valueMm, pickCount and placements: the position and rotation of every picked part after the solve. A pick that does not resolve is unknown_part / unknown_face, and a joint the solver refuses is joint_unsolvable with details.reason and, when more than one axis matches, details.candidates (id, origin, direction, radius); in both cases nothing is written and no card is left open. usedSelection is always false: the picks are explicit. Takes return: "status" | "summary" | "full" (MCP default "status": status.script is omitted; "summary" adds status.features; "full" echoes the script).

picks.description: One row per reference: fixed takes one (a whole part, a face or an edge), every other type takes two, one per part.

face_id.description: Face id from list_faces on that part (e.g. f7). Valid only until the next remesh; pass the key from the same list_faces row with the id.

kind.description: Pick kind when key is explicit (concentric uses axis picks). part picks the whole part, for a fixed joint; it needs no face_id or key.

return.description: How much of status to return: "status" drops status.script, "summary" drops it and adds status.features (the feature strip), "full" keeps the whole script. Over MCP the default is "status"; in the page it is "full". Read the script with get_script.

name: joint_create
